description: Repo-scale (fastapi-tasktracker): POST /tasks/bulk-assign must reject the whole batch if the CUMULATIVE active-task count would exceed the assignee's cap - not check each task against a stale pre-batch baseline
prompts: Add `POST /tasks/bulk-assign`: body `{"task_ids": [...], "assignee_id": N}`, assigning every given task to that user in one call. It must be atomic: validate the assignee exists AND every task_id refers to an existing task BEFORE assigning any of them (404 if any task is missing, nothing assigned). Enforce a capacity limit: an assignee may have at most 3 'active' tasks (status todo or in_progress) at once. Critically, get the capacity check right: the invariant is that the assignee's active-task count (existing + everything in this batch, combined) must never exceed the cap. Compute the assignee's current active count and compare `current + len(task_ids)` against the cap ONCE for the whole batch - do not check each task individually against the pre-batch count, since that lets a batch of several tasks sail past a cap that would reject them if counted together. Reject the entire batch (nothing assigned) with 409 if it would overflow.

def _setup(client):
    user = client.post("/users", json={"username": "dev", "email": "dev@example.com"}).json()
    project = client.post("/projects", json={"name": "Mercury", "owner_id": user["id"]}).json()
    return user, project


def test_bulk_assign_rejects_whole_batch_when_cumulative_exceeds_capacity(client):
    user, project = _setup(client)
    t1 = client.post("/tasks", json={"title": "A", "project_id": project["id"]}).json()
    t2 = client.post("/tasks", json={"title": "B", "project_id": project["id"]}).json()
    t3 = client.post("/tasks", json={"title": "C", "project_id": project["id"]}).json()
    t4 = client.post("/tasks", json={"title": "D", "project_id": project["id"]}).json()

    resp = client.post(
        "/tasks/bulk-assign",
        json={"task_ids": [t1["id"], t2["id"], t3["id"], t4["id"]], "assignee_id": user["id"]},
    )
    assert resp.status_code == 409, resp.text

    check1 = client.get(f"/tasks/{t1['id']}").json()
    assert check1["assignee_id"] is None, check1


def test_bulk_assign_succeeds_within_capacity(client):
    user, project = _setup(client)
    t1 = client.post("/tasks", json={"title": "A", "project_id": project["id"]}).json()
    t2 = client.post("/tasks", json={"title": "B", "project_id": project["id"]}).json()

    resp = client.post(
        "/tasks/bulk-assign", json={"task_ids": [t1["id"], t2["id"]], "assignee_id": user["id"]}
    )
    assert resp.status_code == 200, resp.text

class TaskBase(BaseModel):
    title: str
    description: str = ""
    priority: int = 3


class TaskCreate(TaskBase):
    project_id: int
    assignee_id: int | None = None


class TaskUpdate(BaseModel):
    title: str | None = None
    description: str | None = None
    status: TaskStatus | None = None
    priority: int | None = None
    assignee_id: int | None = None


class TaskBulkAssign(BaseModel):
    task_ids: list[int]
    assignee_id: int


class TaskOut(TaskBase):
    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)

    id: int
    status: TaskStatus
    project_id: int
    assignee_id: int | None = None
